extraction_notes.note: The \\label proporthogonality is used for both Proposition 4.61 and Proposition 4.68; the \\ref in the proof of Proposition 4.70 means 4.68 but resolves to 4.61, so a named edge from 4.68 was added by hand and the ref edge from 4.61 is a wrong_ref artefact.
Lemma 2.1(iii) says 'both conditions (ii) and (iii)', evidently meaning (i) and (ii); copied verbatim.

Several results without a proof environment (Theorems 2.13, 3.7, Proposition 2.21, Corollaries 2.24-2.25, Propositions 4.13, 4.15, 4.19, 7.16) are argued in the preceding discussion; those paragraphs were taken as prose proof nodes.

Step rule 7 nesting of inline 'Let us show/check' claims was applied where the claim and its argument form a contiguous block; in long labelled parts (e.g. Proposition 2.5(i), Lemma 3.12(vi)) the label steps were kept without child steps.

Proposition 6.11 (coinduced topology) and Definition 3.2 (morphism of sites) were marked external since the paper attributes them to the Elephant and SGA4, although it gives its own proof/formulation.
Some remark environments introduce terms used later ($J$-bicovering arrows, ${\\cal C}^{cart}_p$, $\\Sigma^{\\cal E}_u$); these were added as definition nodes nested in the remarks.

nodes.name: Small-generated site
nodes.statement: Recall that a \emph{small-generated site} (in the sense of \cite{Shulman}) (also called an \emph{essentially small site} in \cite{El}) is a site $({\cal C}, J)$ such that $\cal C$ is locally small and has a small $J$-dense subcategory.
differentia: $\cal C$ is locally small and has a small $J$-dense subcategory

nodes.name: Canonical functor $l_J^{\cal C}$
nodes.statement: For any small-generated site $({\cal C}, J)$, we shall denote by $l_{J}^{{\cal C}}$ (or simply by $l$, when there is no risk of ambiguity) the functor ${\cal C}\to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ given by the composite of the Yoneda embedding $y_{\cal C}:{\cal C}\to [{\cal C}^\textup{op}, {\bf Set }]$ with the associated sheaf functor $a_{J}:[{\cal C}^\textup{op}, {\bf Set }] \to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$.

nodes.name: $J$-covering family
nodes.statement: We shall say that a family of arrows in $\cal C$ with common codomain is $J$-covering if the sieve generated by it is.

nodes.name: Unit $\eta_J$ of the sheafification adjunction
nodes.statement: The unit of the adjunction between the inclusion functor $i$ of ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ into $[{\cal C}^\textup{op}, {\bf Set }]$ and the associated sheaf functor $a_{J}$ will be denoted by $\eta_{J}$ (or simply by $\eta$).

nodes.name: Closure operation $c_J$
nodes.statement: Notice that we have a closure operation $c_{J}$ on subobjects in the presheaf category $[{\cal C}^\textup{op}, {\bf Set }]$, which admits the following explicit description: for any subobject $A\rightarrowtail E$ in $[{\cal C}^\textup{op}, {\bf Set }]$, we have \[ c_{J}(A)(c)=\{x\in E(c) \mid \{f:d\to c \mid E(f)(x)\in A(d)\}\in J(c)\} \] for any $c\in {\cal C}$.
nodes.statement_short: The closure $c_J(A)$ consists of elements whose sieve of restrictions landing in $A$ is $J$-covering.

nodes.name: Existence of the associated sheaf functor for small-generated sites
nodes.statement: Note also that, for any small-generated site $({\cal C}, J)$, the canonical inclusion functor ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)\hookrightarrow [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ admits a left adjoint $a_{J}$, which we call, by analogy with the classical case, the associated sheaf functor, and which is (colimit and) finite-limit-preserving.
assumptions: for any small-generated site $({\cal C}, J)$
conclusions: the canonical inclusion functor ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)\hookrightarrow [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ admits a left adjoint $a_{J}$

nodes.name: Proof of existence of $a_J$
nodes.statement: Indeed, if $\cal D$ is a $J$-dense small subcategory of $\cal C$ then, by the Comparison Lemma, we have an equivalence $c:{\bf Sh}({\cal D}, J|_{\cal D})\to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ which is the restriction, along the inclusions ${\bf Sh}({\cal D}, J|_{\cal D})\hookrightarrow [{\cal D}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ and ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)\hookrightarrow [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$, of the functor $[{\cal D}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]\to [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ given by the right Kan extension along the embedding $i$ of ${\cal D}^{\textup{op}}$ into ${\cal C}^{\textup{op}}$, whence the composite functor $c\circ a_{J|_{\cal D}}\circ (-\circ i):[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }] \to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ yields a left adjoint to the inclusion ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)\hookrightarrow [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$.
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to a small dense subcategory and use the Comparison Lemma.

nodes.name: Site characterization of monos, epis and isos in a sheaf topos
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $\alpha:F\to G$ an arrow in the presheaf category $[{\cal C}^\textup{op}, {\bf Set }]$. Then \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $a_{J}(\alpha)$ is a monomorphism in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ if and only if for every $c\in {\cal C}$ and any elements $x, x'\in F(c)$ such that $\alpha(c)(x)=\alpha(c)(x')$, the sieve $\{f:d\to c \mid F(f)(x)=F(f)(x')\}$ is $J$-covering. \item $a_{J}(\alpha)$ is an epimorphism in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ if and only if for every $c\in {\cal C}$ and $x\in G(c)$, the sieve $\{f:d\to c \mid G(f)(x)\in \textup{Im}(\alpha(d)) \}$ is $J$-covering. \item $a_{J}(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ if and only if both conditions (ii) and (iii) are satisfied. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $a_J(\alpha)$ is mono/epi/iso iff explicit $J$-covering conditions on sieves of elements hold.
assumptions: $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $\alpha:F\to G$ an arrow in the presheaf category $[{\cal C}^\textup{op}, {\bf Set }]$
conclusions: $a_{J}(\alpha)$ is a monomorphism in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ if and only if for every $c\in {\cal C}$ and any elements $x, x'\in F(c)$ such that $\alpha(c)(x)=\alpha(c)(x')$, the sieve $\{f:d\to c \mid F(f)(x)=F(f)(x')\}$ is $J$-covering.

$a_{J}(\alpha)$ is an epimorphism in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ if and only if for every $c\in {\cal C}$ and $x\in G(c)$, the sieve $\{f:d\to c \mid G(f)(x)\in \textup{Im}(\alpha(d)) \}$ is $J$-covering.
$a_{J}(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ if and only if both conditions (ii) and (iii) are satisfied.
nodes.label: lemmalift

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1 (Site characterization of monos, epis and isos in a sheaf topos)
nodes.statement: (i) An arrow $A\to B$ in a category with pullbacks is a monomorphism if and only if the diagonal monomorphism $A\to A\times_{B} A$ is an isomorphism. We can thus conclude that $a_{J}(\alpha)$ is a monomorphism in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ if and only if the diagonal arrow $F\to F\times_{G} F$ is $c_{J}$-dense, that is if and only if for every $c\in {\cal C}$ and any elements $x, x'\in F(c)$ such that $\alpha(c)(x)=\alpha(c)(x')$, the sieve $\{f:d\to c \mid F(f)(x)=F(f)(x')\}$ is $J$-covering. (ii) Clearly, $\alpha$ is sent by $a_{J}$ to an epimorphism if and only if its image $\textup{Im}(\alpha)$ is $c_{J}$-dense, that is if and only if, for every $c\in {\cal C}$ and $x\in G(c)$, the sieve $\{f:d\to c \mid G(f)(x)\in \textup{Im}(\alpha(d)) \}$ is $J$-covering. (iii) This follows from the fact that every topos is a balanced category.
nodes.statement_short: Translate mono/epi/iso of $a_J(\alpha)$ into $c_J$-density conditions; iso case by balancedness.

nodes.name: Remarks on the epimorphism criterion and $J$-bicovering arrows
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item Let $A_{c, x}:=\{f:d\to c \mid G(f)(x)\in \textup{Im}(\alpha(d)) \}$ (for each $c\in {\cal C}$ and $x\in G(c)$). Then for any arrow $\xi:c\to c'$ and any elements $x\in G(c)$ and $x'\in G(c')$ such that $G(\xi)(x')=x$, $A_{c, x}=\xi^{\ast}(A_{c', x'})$. So, if the codomain of $\alpha$ is a representable $y_{\cal C}(c)$, condition (ii) becomes equivalent to the requirement that the sieve $\{f:d\to c \mid f\in \textup{Im}(\alpha(d))\}$ be $J$-covering. \item The arrows of $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ whose image under the associated sheaf functor $a_{J}$ is an isomorphism will be called \emph{$J$-bicovering}, in comformity with the terminology `` \emph{bicouvrante}'' introduced in section II.5 of \cite{grothendieck} for qualifying this type of arrows. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Stability of the sieves $A_{c,x}$ under pullback; arrows inverted by $a_J$ are called $J$-bicovering.

nodes.name: $J$-bicovering arrow
nodes.statement: The arrows of $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ whose image under the associated sheaf functor $a_{J}$ is an isomorphism will be called \emph{$J$-bicovering}, in comformity with the terminology `` \emph{bicouvrante}'' introduced in section II.5 of \cite{grothendieck} for qualifying this type of arrows.
differentia: whose image under the associated sheaf functor $a_{J}$ is an isomorphism

nodes.name: Subobjects of a sheafification and $c_J$-closed subobjects
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site. Then for any object $F$ of $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$, denoting by $\textup{ClSub}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(F)$ the sub-lattice of ${\rm Sub}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(F)$ consisting of the $c_J$-closed subobjects, we have a lattice isomorphism \[ {\rm Sub}_{{\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)}(a_{J}(F))\simeq \textup{ClSub}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(F) \] which sends a subobject in $\textup{ClSub}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(F)$ to its image under $a_{J}$ and a subobject of $a_{J}(F)$ to the pullback of it under the unit arrow $F\to a_{J}(F)$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathrm{Sub}(a_J(F))$ is isomorphic to the lattice of $c_J$-closed subobjects of $F$.
assumptions: $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site
conclusions: we have a lattice isomorphism
nodes.label: propclosedsubobjects

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.3 (Subobjects of a sheafification and $c_J$-closed subobjects)
nodes.statement: Given a subobject $m:A\to a_{J}(F)$ in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$, let us associate with it the subobject $n:A'\rightarrowtail F$ of $F$ defined by the following pullback diagram in $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$: $$ \xymatrix{ A' \ar[d]^{n} \ar[r] & \ar[d]^{m} A \\ F \ar[r]^{\eta_{F}\:\:} & a_{J}(F) } $$ Recall that the $c_{J}$-closure $c_{J}(k):A''\rightarrowtail F$ of a subobject $k:A'\rightarrowtail F$ in $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ is characterized by the following pullback diagram: $$ \xymatrix{ A'' \ar[d]^{c_J(k)} \ar[r] & \ar[d]^{a_{J}(k)} a_J(A') \\ F \ar[r]^{\eta_{F}\:\:} & a_{J}(F) } $$ It thus follows that $n$ is $c_J$-closed, since by applying the pullback-preserving functor $a_J$ to the former pullback square we obtain that $m\cong a_J(n)$. Conversely, we associate with any $c_J$-closed subobject $n$ the subobject $a_J(n)$ of ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$. It is immediate to see that these two operations are inverse to each other, and that they are order-preserving; so they are lattice isomorphisms.
nodes.statement_short: Pull back subobjects along the unit and use the pullback characterization of $c_J$-closure.

nodes.name: Remarks on images and the elementary-topos generalization
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item Given an arrow $\alpha:P\to Q$ in $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$, the $c_J$-closed subobject $Q_{\alpha}$ of $Q$ corresponding via Proposition \ref{propclosedsubobjects} to the image of the arrow $a_{J}(\alpha)$ is given by $$Q_{\alpha}(c)=\{x\in Q(c) \mid \{f:d\to c \mid Q(f)(x)\in \textup{Im}(\alpha(d))\}\in J(c) \}$$ for any $c\in {\cal C}$. \item Proposition \ref{propclosedsubobjects} clearly generalizes to the setting of elementary toposes, replacing $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ by an arbitrary elementary topos $\cal E$, $J$ by a local operator on it and $c_{J}$ by the associate closure operation on subobjects in $\cal E$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Explicit description of the closed subobject $Q_\alpha$ corresponding to the image of $a_J(\alpha)$; generalization to elementary toposes.
nodes.label: remimageclosedsubobject

nodes.name: $J$-local equality
nodes.statement: Given a site $({\cal C}, J)$, for two arrows $h,k:c\to d$ in $\cal C$ we shall write $h\equiv_{J} k$ for \emph{$J$-local equality}, that is, to mean that there exists a $J$-covering sieve $S$ on $c$ such that $h\circ f=k\circ f$ for every $f\in S$.
nodes.section: 2.3 Site-theoretic description of arrows between objects coming from the site

nodes.name: $l$ identifies exactly the locally equal arrows
nodes.statement: Notice that $l(h)=l(k)$ if and only if $h\equiv_{J} k$.
nodes.section: 2.3 Site-theoretic description of arrows between objects coming from the site
conclusions: $l(h)=l(k)$ if and only if $h\equiv_{J} k$
equivalent_conditions: $h\equiv_{J} k$

nodes.name: Local representation of arrows between objects from the site
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item Then for any arrow $\xi:l(c)\to l(d)$ in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ there exists a family of arrows $\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c, g_{u}:c_{u}\to d \mid u\in U\}$ such that $\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c \mid u\in U\}$ generates a $J$-covering sieve, for any object $e$ and arrows $h:e\to c_{u}$ and $k:e\to c_{u'}$ such that $f_{u}\circ h=f_{u'}\circ k$ we have $g_{u}\circ h\equiv_{J} g_{u'}\circ k$, and $\xi \circ l(f_{u})=l(g_{u})$ for every $u\in U$. \item Conversely, any family of arrows ${\cal F}:\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c, g_{u}:c_{u}\to d \mid u\in U\}$ such that $\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c \mid u\in U\}$ generates a $J$-covering sieve and for any object $e$ and arrows $h:e\to c_{u}$ and $k:e\to c_{u'}$ such that $f_{u}\circ h=f_{u'}\circ k$ we have $g_{u}\circ h\equiv_{J} g_{u'}\circ k$, determines a unique arrow $\xi_{\cal F}:l(c)\to l(d)$ in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ such that $\xi_{\cal F}\circ l(f_{u})=l(g_{u})$ for every $u\in U$. \item Two families ${\cal F}=\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c, g_{u}:c_{u}\to d \mid u\in U\}$ and ${\cal F}'=\{f'_{v}:e_{v}\to c, g'_{v}:e_{v}\to d \mid v\in V\}$ as in (ii) determine the same arrow $l(c)\to l(d)$ (i.e. $\xi_{\cal F}=\xi_{{\cal F}'}$) if and only if there exist a $J$-covering family $\{a_{k}:b_{k}\to c \mid k\in K\}$ and factorizations of it through both of them by arrows $x_{k}:b_{k}\to c_{u(k)}$ and $y_{k}:b_{k}\to e_{v(k)}$ (i.e. $f_{u(k)}\circ x_{k}=a_{k}=f'_{v(k)}\circ y_{k}$ for every $k\in K$) such that $g_{u(k)}\circ x_{k}\equiv_{J} g'_{v(k)}\circ y_{k}$ for every $k\in K$. \item Given two families ${\cal F}=\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c, g_{u}:c_{u}\to d \mid u\in U\}$ and ${\cal G}=\{h_{v}:d_{v}\to d, k_{v}:d_{v}\to e \mid v\in V\}$, the composite arrow $\xi_{\cal G}\circ \xi_{\cal F}:l(c)\to l(e)$ is induced as in (ii) by the family $\{f_{u}\circ x:\textup{dom}(x)\to c, k_{v}\circ y:\textup{dom}(y)\to e \mid (u,v,x,y )\in Z\}$, where $Z=\{(u, v, x, y) \mid u\in U, v\in V, \textup{dom}(x)=\textup{dom}(y), \textup{cod}(x)=c_{u}, \textup{cod}(y)=d_{v}, h_{v}\circ y=g_{u}\circ x\}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Arrows $l(c)\to l(d)$ in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C},J)$ correspond to compatible families of spans with $J$-covering first legs, up to local equivalence; composition described explicitly.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.5 (Local representation of arrows between objects from the site)
nodes.statement: (i) Consider the following pullback square in $[{\cal C}^\textup{op}, {\bf Set }]$: $$ \xymatrix{ R \ar[d]^{r} \ar[rr]^t & & y_{\cal C}(d) \ar[d]^{\eta_{y_{\cal C}(d)}} \\ y_{\cal C}(c) \ar[rr]^{\xi\circ \eta_{y_{\cal C}(c)}} & & l(d) } $$ and the sieve $S=\{f:e\to c \mid \exists g:e\to d \textup{ with } (f, g)\in R\}$ on $c$ given by the image in $[{\cal C}^\textup{op}, {\bf Set }]$ of the arrow $r:R\to y_{\cal C}(c)$. This sieve is $J$-covering since it is sent by $a_{J}$ to an isomorphism. Let us show that for any $(f,g)\in R$, $\xi\circ l(f)=l(g)$. Consider the adjunction between $i$ and $a_{J}$: the arrow $\eta_{y_{\cal C}(d)} \circ y_{\cal C}(g)$ is the transpose of $l(g)$ and the arrow $\xi\circ \eta_{y_{\cal C}(c)} \circ y_{\cal C}(f)$ is the transpose of $\xi \circ l(f)$, so it is equivalent to verify that $\eta_{y_{\cal C}(d)} \circ y_{\cal C}(g)=\xi\circ \eta_{y_{\cal C}(c)} \circ y_{\cal C}(f)$. But this follows by the commutativity of the above square, since $(f, g)\in R$. To check that the family of arrows $\{(f, g) \mid (f,g)\in R\}$ satisfies the required condition, we have to check that for any $(f, g), (f',g')\in R$ and arrows $h, h'$ such that $f\circ h=f'\circ h'$, $g\circ h\equiv_{J} g'\circ h'$, equivalently $l(g\circ h)=l(g'\circ h')$. Since $(f\circ h, g\circ h)\in R$ as $R$ is functorial, we have $\xi\circ l(f\circ h)=l(g\circ h)$; similarly, we have $\xi \circ l(f'\circ h')=l(g'\circ h')$. So $l(g\circ h)=l(g'\circ h')$, as required. (ii) Any sieve $S$ on an object $c$ of $\cal C$, regarded as a presheaf on ${\cal C}$, is the colimit of the canonical diagram defined on the full subcategory $\int S$ of ${\cal C}\slash c$ on the objects which are elements of $S$. If $S$ is $J$-covering then the canonical momonomorphism $S\rightarrowtail y_{\cal C}(c)$ is sent by the associated sheaf functor $a_{J}$ to an isomorphism, so, since $a_{J}$ is colimit-preserving, $l(c)$ is the colimit of the functor $a_{S}:\int S \to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ sending any object $f:d\to c$ of $\int S$ to $l(d)$ and any arrow $h:(f:d\to c)\to (f':d'\to c)$ in $\int S$ to $l(h):l(d')\to l(d)$. Therefore, giving an arrow $l(c)\to l(d)$ in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ amounts to giving a cocone on $a_{S}$ with vertex $l(d)$. Any family of arrows $\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c, g_{u}:c_{u}\to d \mid u\in U\}$ such that $\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c \mid u\in U\}$ generates a $J$-covering sieve and for any object $e$ and arrows $h:e\to c_{u}$ and $k:e\to c_{u'}$ such that $f_{u}\circ h=f_{u'}\circ k$ we have $g_{u}\circ h\equiv_{J} g_{u'}\circ k$, defines such a cocone. Indeed, by taking $S$ equal to the sieve generated by the family $\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c\}$ we obtain, thanks to the property that for any object $e$ and arrows $h:e\to c_{u}$ and $k:e\to c_{u'}$ such that $f_{u}\circ h=f_{u'}\circ k$ we have $g_{u}\circ h\equiv_{J} g_{u'}\circ k$, a well-defined family of arrows $l(\textup{dom}(f))\to l(d)$ (for $f\in S$) satisfying the commutativity conditions for a cocone. It is clear that the arrow $l(c)\to l(d)$ thus defined satisfies the required property. (iii) Let us first prove the `if' direction. Since the sieve generated by the family $\{a_{k}:b_{k}\to c \mid k\in K\}$ is $J$-covering, the arrows $l(a_{k})$ to $l(c)$ are jointly epimorphic and hence $\xi_{\cal F}=\xi_{{\cal F}'}$ if and only if $\xi_{\cal F}\circ l(a_{k})=\xi_{{\cal F}'}\circ l(a_{k})$ for every $k\in K$. But $\xi_{\cal F}\circ l(a_{k})=\xi_{\cal F} \circ l(f_{u(k)})\circ l(x_{k})= l(g_{u(k)})\circ l(x_{k})=l(g_{u(k)}\circ x_{k})=l(g'_{v(k)}\circ y_{k})=l(g'_{v(k)})\circ l(y_{k})=\xi_{{\cal F}'}\circ l(f'_{v(k)})\circ l(y_{k})=\xi_{{\cal F}'}\circ l(a_{k})$, where the equality $l(g_{u(k)}\circ x_{k})=l(g'_{v(k)}\circ y_{k})$ follows from the fact that $g_{u(k)}\circ x_{k}\equiv_{J} g'_{v(k)}\circ y_{k}$. It thus remains to prove the `only if' direction. Suppose that $\xi_{\cal F}=\xi_{{\cal F}'}$. Let us define the family $\{a_{k}:b_{k}\to c \mid k\in K\}$ to be the intersection of the sieve generated by the family $\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c \mid u\in U\}$ with that generated by the family $\{f'_{v}:e_{v}\to c \mid v\in V\}$; since these two sieves are $J$-covering by our hypotheses, their intersection is $J$-covering as well. Let us choose factorizations $x_{k}:b_{k}\to c_{u(k)}$ and $y_{k}:b_{k}\to e_{v(k)}$ of it through the arrows of these families, so that $f_{u(k)}\circ x_{k}=a_{k}=f'_{v(k)}\circ y_{k}$ for every $k\in K$. We want to prove that, for every $k\in K$, $g_{u(k)}\circ x_{k}\equiv_{J} g'_{v(k)}\circ y_{k}$, equivalently that $l(g_{u(k)}\circ x_{k})=l(g'_{v(k)}\circ y_{k})$. But $l(g_{u(k)}\circ x_{k})=l(g_{u(k)})\circ l(x_{k})=\xi_{\cal F}\circ l(f_{u(k)})\circ l(x_{k})=\xi_{{\cal F}'}\circ l(f'_{v(k)}\circ y_{k})=l(g'_{v(k)}\circ y_{k})$, as required. (iv) First of all, we have to show that the family of arrows $\{f_{u}\circ x \mid (u,v,x,y )\in Z\}$ is $J$-covering. To this end, consider the pullback $$ \xymatrix{ P \ar[d] \ar[r] & H \ar[d] \\ G \ar[r] & y_{\cal C}(d) } $$ where $H$ is the sieve on $d$ generated by the arrows $\{h_{v}:d_{v}\to d \mid v\in I\}$, $G$ is the sieve on $d$ generated by the arrows $\{g_{u}:c_{u}\to d \mid u\in U\}$ and the arrows are the canonical inclusion monomorphisms. Since $H$ is $J$-covering, the canonical monomorphism $H\to y_{\cal C}(d)$ is $c_{J}$-dense and hence the monomorphism $P\rightarrowtail G$ in the above square is $c_{J}$-dense too; this means that for any $u\in U$, the sieve $\{\xi:\textup{dom}(\xi)\to c_{u} \mid g_{u}\circ \xi\in P\}$ is $J$-covering. But $P=H\cap G$, so this means that for any $u\in U$, the sieve $\{x:\textup{dom}(x)\to c_{u} \mid \exists v\,\exists y\,(u,v,x,y)\in Z\}$ is $J$-covering. Since this sieve is contained in the pullback along $f_{u}$ of the sieve $\{f_{u}\circ x \mid (u,v,x,y )\in Z\}$, it follows from the transitivity axiom for Grothendieck topologies that this latter sieve is $J$-covering, as desired. To conclude the proof of (iv), we have to verify that for every $(u,v,x,y)\in Z$, $\xi_{\cal G}\circ \xi_{\cal F}\circ l(f_{u})\circ l(x)=l(k_{v})\circ l(y)$. Recalling the definitions of $\xi_{\cal F}$ and $\xi_{\cal G}$, we obtain that $\xi_{\cal G}\circ \xi_{\cal F}\circ l(f_{u})\circ l(x)=\xi_{\cal G}\circ l(g_{u})\circ l(x)=\xi_{\cal G}\circ l(h_{v})\circ l(y)=l(k_{v})\circ l(y)=l(k_{v}\circ y)$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: Represent $l(c)$ as a colimit over covering sieves and translate arrows into compatible local families.
nodes.section: 2.3 Site-theoretic description of arrows between objects coming from the site

nodes.name: Remarks on the local representation of arrows
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item Proposition \ref{propexplicit} could alternatively have been derived from the description of the topos ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ as a completion of the site $({\cal C}, J)$ provided by Theorem 8.22 \cite{Shulman}. \item If we assume the axiom of choice, given a family of arrows $\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c, g_{u}:c_{u}\to d \mid u\in U\}$ such that $\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c \mid u\in U\}$ generates a $J$-covering sieve and for any object $e$ and arrows $h:e\to c_{u}$ and $k:e\to c_{u'}$ such that $f_{u}\circ h=f_{u'}\circ k$ we have $g_{u}\circ h=g_{u'}\circ k$, as in points (i) and (ii) of Proposition \ref{propexplicit}, we can clearly suppose without loss of generality $U$ to be the $J$-covering sieve on $c$ generated by the family $\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c \mid u\in U\}$. So such a family can be equivalently identified with a family of arrows $g_{f}:\textup{dom}(f)\to d$ indexed by the arrows $f$ of a $J$-covering sieve $S$ on $c$ with the property that for any arrow $h$ composable with $f$, $g_{f\circ h}\equiv_{J} g_{f}\circ h$. \item Under the identification of Remark \ref{rempropexplicit}(b), the family $\{a_{k}:b_{k}\to c \mid k\in K\}$ in point (iii) of Proposition \ref{propexplicit} can be assumed to be the intersection of the sieves $U$ and $V$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Alternative derivation via Shulman's completion; with choice families may be indexed by a covering sieve.
nodes.section: 2.3 Site-theoretic description of arrows between objects coming from the site
nodes.label: rempropexplicit

nodes.name: Factorization of an arrow through $l(h)$
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $h:c\to d, k:c\to e$ arrows in $\cal C$. Then there exists an arrow $\xi:l(e)\to l(d)$ such that $\xi \circ l(h)=l(k)$ if and only if there exists a family of arrows $g_{f}:\textup{dom}(f)\to d$ indexed by the arrows $f$ of a $J$-covering sieve $S$ on $e$ such that $g_{f\circ z}=g_{f}\circ z$ whenever $z$ is composable with $f$, and such that for any $\chi\in h^{\ast}(S)$, $k\circ \chi\equiv_{J} g_{h\circ \chi}$.
nodes.statement_short: Existence of $\xi$ with $\xi\circ l(h)=l(k)$ characterized by a compatible family on a covering sieve.
nodes.section: 2.3 Site-theoretic description of arrows between objects coming from the site
assumptions: $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $h:c\to d, k:c\to e$ arrows in $\cal C$
conclusions: there exists an arrow $\xi:l(e)\to l(d)$ such that $\xi \circ l(h)=l(k)$ if and only if there exists a family of arrows

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.7 (Factorization of an arrow through $l(h)$)
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{propexplicit}, giving an arrow $\xi:l(e)\to l(d)$ amounts to specifying a family of arrows $g_{f}:\textup{dom}(f)\to d$ indexed by the arrows $f$ of a $J$-covering sieve $S$ on $e$ such that $g_{f\circ z}=g_{f}\circ z$ whenever $z$ is composable with $f$, which satisfies $\xi\circ l(f)=l(g_{f})$ for each $f\in S$. Now, $\xi \circ l(h)=l(k)$ if and only if $\xi \circ l(h)\circ l(\chi)=l(k)\circ l(\chi)$ for every $\chi\in h^{\ast}(S)$ (since, $h^{\ast}(S)$ being $J$-covering as $S$ is, the arrows $l(\chi)$ are jointly epimorphic). But $\xi \circ l(h)\circ l(\chi)=\xi \circ l(h\circ \chi)=l(g_{h\circ \chi})$, while $l(k)\circ l(\chi)=l(k\circ \chi)$, so the condition $\xi \circ l(h)=l(k)$ is equivalent to $k\circ \chi\equiv_{J} g_{h\circ \chi}$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Proposition 2.5 and test the equation on a jointly epimorphic covering family.
nodes.section: 2.3 Site-theoretic description of arrows between objects coming from the site

nodes.name: Lifting of arrows into $l(c)$ to the site
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $\xi:A\to l(c)$ an arrow of ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$. Then the family of arrows $\chi:l(d)\to A$, where $d\in {\cal C}$, such that $\xi \circ \chi=l(f)$ for some arrow $f:d\to c$ in $\cal C$ is epimorphic on $A$.
nodes.statement_short: For $\xi:A\to l(c)$, arrows $\chi:l(d)\to A$ with $\xi\circ\chi=l(f)$ form an epimorphic family.
nodes.section: 2.3 Site-theoretic description of arrows between objects coming from the site
assumptions: $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $\xi:A\to l(c)$ an arrow of ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$
conclusions: the family of arrows $\chi:l(d)\to A$, where $d\in {\cal C}$, such that $\xi \circ \chi=l(f)$ for some arrow $f:d\to c$ in $\cal C$ is epimorphic on $A$
nodes.label: proplifttosite

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.8 (Lifting of arrows into $l(c)$ to the site)
nodes.statement: The family $R$ of arrows to $A$ whose domain is of the form $l(e)$ for some $e\in {\cal C}$ is clearly epimorphic on $A$. Let us denote by $T$ the family of arrows $\chi:l(d)\to A$, where $d\in {\cal C}$, such that $\xi \circ \chi=l(f)$ for some arrow $f:d\to c$ in $\cal C$. To show that $T$ is epimorphic, it clearly suffices, by transitivity, to show that for any $\alpha\in R$, $\alpha^{\ast}(T)$ is epimorphic. But this follows from Proposition \ref{propexplicit}(i) applied to the arrow $\xi \circ \alpha$, since that implies that there exists a $J$-covering family $\{f_{i} \mid i\in I\}$ of arrows on $\textup{dom}(\alpha)$ and for each $i\in I$ an arrow $g_{i}:\textup{dom}(f_{i})\to c$ such that $\xi\circ \alpha \circ l(f_{i})=l(g_{i})$; indeed, the family of arrows $\{l(f_{i}) \mid i\in I\}$ is epimorphic and contained in $\alpha^{\ast}(T)$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce by transitivity of epimorphic families and apply Proposition 2.5(i).
nodes.section: 2.3 Site-theoretic description of arrows between objects coming from the site

nodes.name: Relative topology on elements of a presheaf
nodes.statement: If $A=a_{J}(P)$ for a presheaf $P$ on $\cal C$ then the collection of objects $(d, x)$ of of the category $\int P$ of elements of $P$ such that, denoting by $\lambda_{(d, x)}:l(d)\to a_{J}(P)=A$ the canonical colimit arrow, $\xi\circ \lambda_{(d, x)}$ is of the form $l(f)$ for some $f:d\to c$ defines a full $J_{P}$-dense subcategory of $\int P$ (where $J_{P}$ is the Grothendieck topology on $\int P$ whose covering sieves are precisely those sent by the canonical projection functor ${\int P}\to {\cal C}$ to $J$-covering sieves).
nodes.statement_short: Objects of $\int P$ whose colimit arrow composed with $\xi$ comes from the site form a $J_P$-dense subcategory.
nodes.section: 2.3 Site-theoretic description of arrows between objects coming from the site
nodes.label: remrelativetopology

nodes.name: $J$-functional relation
nodes.statement: In a presheaf topos $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$, a relation $R\rightarrowtail P\times Q$ (that is, an assignment $c\to R(c)$ to each object $c$ of $\cal C$ of a subset $R(c)$ of $P(c)\times Q(c)$ which is \emph{functorial} in the sense that for any arrow $f:c\to c'$ in $\cal C$, $P(f)\times Q(f)$ sends $R(c')$ to $R(c)$), is said to be \emph{$J$-functional from $P$ to $Q$} if it satisfies the following properties: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item for any $c\in {\cal C}$ and any $(x, y)\in P(c)\times Q(c)$,\\ if $\{f:d\to c \mid\ (P(f)(x), Q(f)(y))\in R(d)\}\in J(c)$ then $(x,y)\in R(c)$; \item for any $c\in {\cal C}$ and any $(x, y), (x', y')\in R(c)$, if $x=x'$ then $\{f:d\to c \mid Q(f)(y)=Q(f)(y')\}\in J(c)$; \item for any $c\in {\cal C}$ and any $x\in P(c)$, $\{f:d\to c \mid \exists y\in Q(d) \,(P(f)(x), y)\in R(d) \}\in J(c)$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: A relation of presheaves which is $J$-closed, locally single-valued and locally total.
nodes.label: defJfunctionalrelation

nodes.name: Remarks on $J$-functional relations
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item By the above discussion, the $J$-functional relations $R\rightarrowtail P\times Q$ from $P$ to $Q$ are precisely the $c_{J}$-closed relations $R$ on $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ whose image under $a_{J}$ is the graph of an arrow $a_{J}(P)\to a_{J}(Q)$ in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$, that is the subobjects corresponding to the functional relations from $a_{J}(P)$ to $a_{J}(Q)$ under the bijection of Proposition \ref{propclosedsubobjects}. \item Any relation $R\rightarrowtail P\times Q$ on $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ satisfying conditions (ii) and (iii) of Definition \ref{defJfunctionalrelation} admits a \emph{$J$-closure} $\overline{R}^{J}$, consisting of all the pairs $(x, y)\in P(c)\times Q(c)$ such that $\{f:d\to c \mid\ (P(f)(x), Q(f)(y))\in R(d)\}\in J(c)$, which satisfies all the conditions of the definition. \item The $J$-functional relation $R_{\xi}$ corresponding to an arrow $\xi:a_{J}(P)\to a_{J}(Q)$ can be concretely described as follows: for any $(x,y)\in P(c)\times Q(c)$, $(x, y)\in R_{\xi}$ if and only if $(\xi\circ \eta_{P})(c)(x)=(\eta_{Q}(c))(y)$, where $\eta_{P}:P\to a_{J}(P)$ and $\eta_{Q}:Q\to a_{J}(Q)$ are the unit arrows. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $J$-functional relations are the closed relations whose sheafification is a graph; $J$-closure; explicit relation $R_\xi$ of an arrow.
nodes.label: remfunctionalrelations

nodes.name: $J$-functional relations as functorial assignments of equivalence classes
nodes.statement: We have a natural bijection between the $J$-functional relations $R$ from $P$ to $Q$ and the functions $f$ assigning to each element $x\in P(c)$ a $\equiv_{J}$-equivalence class of elements of $Q(c)$ (that is, a subset $A$ of $Q(c)$ such that for any $y\in A$ and $y'\in Q(c)$, $y\equiv_{J} y'$ if and only if $y'\in A$) which is \emph{functorial} in the sense that for any arrow $g:d\to c$ in $\cal C$, if $y\in f(x)$ then $Q(g)(y)\in f(P(g)(x))$, \emph{$J$-closed} in the sense that if $Q(g)(y)\in f(P(g)(x))$ for all the arrows $g$ of a $J$-covering sieve then $y\in f(x)$ and \emph{$J$-locally pointed} in the sense that for any $x\in P(c)$, $\{g:d\to c \mid f(P(g)(x))\neq \emptyset \}\in J(c)$. This correspondence sends \begin{itemize} \item a function $f$ satisfying the above properties to the relation $R_{f}\rightarrowtail P\times Q$ consisting of the pairs $(x, y)$ such that $y\in f(x)$; \item a $J$-functional relation $R$ from $P$ to $Q$ to the function $f_{R}$ given by: \[ f_{R}(x)=\{y\in Q(c) \mid (x, y)\in R(c)\} \] for any $x\in P(c)$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: $J$-functional relations from $P$ to $Q$ correspond to functorial, $J$-closed, $J$-locally pointed assignments of $\equiv_J$-classes.
conclusions: We have a natural bijection between the $J$-functional relations $R$ from $P$ to $Q$ and the functions $f$
nodes.label: propfuncionalassignment

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.12 ($J$-functional relations as functorial assignments of equivalence classes)
nodes.statement: First, let us show that the correspondence is well-defined. Given $f$, let us verify that $R_{f}$ is a $J$-functional relation. The functoriality of $R_{f}$ follows from that of $f$. The relation $R_{f}$ satisfies condition (i) by the $J$-closedness of $f$, condition (ii) since $f$ takes values in $\equiv_{J}$-equivalence classes and condition (iii) since $f$ is $J$-locally pointed. Conversely, let us show that, given a $J$-functional relation $R$ from $P$ to $Q$, the function $f_{R}$ takes values in $\equiv_{J}$-equivalence classes, is functorial, $J$-closed and $J$-locally pointed. Given $x\in P(c)$ and $y, y'\in Q(c)$ such that $y\in f_{R}(x)$, let us prove that $y\equiv_{J} y$ if and only if $y'\in f_{R}(x)$. The `if' direction follows at once from the fact that $R$ satisfies condition (ii), so it remains to prove the `only if' one. If $y\equiv_{J} y$ then there is a $J$-covering sieve $T$ on $c$ such that for any $t\in T$, $Q(t)(y)=Q(t)(y')$. Now, since $(x, y)\in R(c)$, by the functoriality of $R$ we have $(P(t)(x), Q(t)(y))\in R(\textup{dom}(t))$ for each $t\in T$; condition (i) thus implies that $(x, y')\in R(c)$, as required. The fact that $f_{R}$ is functorial (resp. $J$-closed, $J$-locally pointed) follows from the fact that $R$ is functorial (resp. satisfies condition (i), condition (iii)). Now that we have proved that the assignments $R \to f_{R}$ and $f \to R_{f}$ are well-defined, it remains to show that they are inverse to each other. The equality $f=f_{R_{f}}$ follows from the fact that for any $x$, $f_{R_{f}}=\{y \mid (x, y)\in R_{f}\}=\{y \mid y\in f(x)\}=f(x)$, while the equality $R=R_{f_{R}}$ follows from the fact that $R_{f_{R}}=\{(x, y) \mid y\in f_{R}(x)\}=R$.
nodes.statement_short: Check both assignments are well defined, then that they are mutually inverse.

nodes.name: Argument for composition of $J$-functional relations
nodes.statement: The $J$-functional relation corresponding to the composite of two arrows in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $J$-functional relations $R$ and $S$ is the $c_{J}$-closure of the relation given by the (relational) composite of $R$ and $S$ in $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$. Indeed, the operation of composition of relations is clearly preserved by geometric functors; but $a_{J}$ is such a functor and, by Proposition \ref{propclosedsubobjects}, there is just one $c_{J}$-closed subobject whose image under $a_{J}$ is a given subobject. Notice that the composition of relations in a presheaf topos is computed pointwise.
nodes.statement_short: Composition of relations is preserved by $a_J$, and closed subobjects are determined by their sheafification (Proposition 2.3).

nodes.name: Arrows between sheafified presheaves as $J$-functional relations
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site. Then, for any presheaves $P,Q\in [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}},{\bf Set }]$, the arrows $a_{J}(P)\to a_{J}(Q)$ in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ are in natural bijection with the $J$-functional relations from $P$ to $Q$ in $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}},{\bf Set }]$. Moreover, under this bijection, the composition of arrows in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ corresponds to the $c_{J}$-closure of the composition in $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}},{\bf Set }]$ of the associated $J$-functional relations. This operation, which we shall denote by the symbol $\ast$, admits the following explicit description: given a $J$-functional relation $R$ from $P$ to $Q$ and a $J$-functional relation $S$ from $Q$ to $Z$, $S\ast R$ is given by the formula \begin{equation*}\begin{split} (S\ast R)(c)&=\{(x, z)\in P(c)\times Z(c) \mid \{f:d\to c \mid \exists y\in Q(d)\, \\ & \quad\quad(P(f)(x), y)\in R(d)\textup{ and } (y, Z(f)(z))\in S(d)\}\in J(c) \} \end{split}\end{equation*} for any $c\in {\cal C}$.
nodes.statement_short: Arrows $a_J(P)\to a_J(Q)$ correspond to $J$-functional relations $P\to Q$, composition being the $c_J$-closure $\ast$ of relational composition.
assumptions: $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site
conclusions: for any presheaves $P,Q\in [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}},{\bf Set }]$, the arrows $a_{J}(P)\to a_{J}(Q)$ in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ are in natural bijection with the $J$-functional relations from $P$ to $Q$ in $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}},{\bf Set }]$. Moreover, under this bijection, the composition of arrows in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ corresponds to the $c_{J}$-closure of the composition in $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}},{\bf Set }]$ of the associated $J$-functional relations. This operation, which we shall denote by the symbol $\ast$, admits the following explicit description: given a $J$-functional relation $R$ from $P$ to $Q$ and a $J$-functional relation $S$ from $Q$ to $Z$, $S\ast R$ is given by the formula \begin{equation*}\begin{split} (S\ast R)(c)&=\{(x, z)\in P(c)\times Z(c) \mid \{f:d\to c \mid \exists y\in Q(d)\, \\ & \quad\quad(P(f)(x), y)\in R(d)\textup{ and } (y, Z(f)(z))\in S(d)\}\in J(c) \} \end{split}\end{equation*} for any $c\in {\cal C}$.
nodes.label: thmfunctionalrelations

nodes.name: Site description of the full subcategory $a_J({\cal C})$
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site. Then the full subcategory $a_{J}({\cal C})$ of ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ on the objects of the form $l(c)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$ is equivalent to the category ${\cal C}_{J}$ defined as follows: \begin{itemize} \item the objects of ${\cal C}_{J}$ are the objects of $\cal C$; \item the arrows $c\to d$ are the collections $R$ of pairs of arrows $(f:e\to c,g:e\to d)$ where $e$ varies among the objects of $\cal C$ (we write $(f, g)\in R(e)$ to mean that $(f, g)\in R$ and $\textup{dom}(f)=\textup{dom}(g)=e$) satisfying the following properties: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item for any arrow $k:e'\to e$, if $(f,g)\in R$ then $(f\circ k, g\circ k)\in R$; \item for any $e\in {\cal C}$ and any arrows $x:e\to c, y:e\to d$, if $\{f:e'\to e \mid\ (x\circ f, y\circ f)\in R\}\in J(e)$ then $(x, y)\in R$; \item for any $e\in {\cal C}$ and any $(x, y), (x', y')\in R(e)$, if $x=x'$ then $\{f:e'\to e \mid y\circ f=y'\circ f\}\in J(e)$; \item for any $e\in {\cal C}$ and any $x:e\to c$, $\{f:e'\to e \mid \exists y:e'\to d \text{ such that } (x\circ f, y)\in R(e') \}\in J(e)$; \end{enumerate} \item the composite $S\ast R$ of two arrows $R:c\to d$ and $S:d\to a$ is given by the following formula: \begin{equation*}\begin{split} (S\ast R)(e)&=\{(x:e\to c, z:e\to a) \mid \{f:e'\to e \mid \exists y:e'\to d\, \\ & \quad\quad(x\circ f, y)\in R(e')\textup{ and } (y, z\circ f)\in S(e')\}\in J(e) \} \end{split}\end{equation*} for any $e\in {\cal C}$. \end{itemize} One half of the equivalence ${\cal C}_{J}\simeq a_{J}({\cal C})$ is given by the functor ${\cal C}_{J}\to a_{J}({\cal C})$ acting on objects by sending any $c\in {\cal C}_{J}$ to $l(c)$ and any arrow $R:c\to c'$ in ${\cal C}_{J}$ to the arrow $l(c)\to l(c')$ in $a_{J}({\cal C})$ whose graph is $a_{J}(R)$.
nodes.statement_short: The full subcategory of objects $l(c)$ is equivalent to the category ${\cal C}_J$ of $J$-functional relations between representables.
assumptions: $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site
conclusions: the full subcategory $a_{J}({\cal C})$ of ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ on the objects of the form $l(c)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$ is equivalent to the category ${\cal C}_{J}$ defined as follows: \begin{itemize} \item the objects of ${\cal C}_{J}$ are the objects of $\cal C$; \item the arrows $c\to d$ are the collections $R$ of pairs of arrows $(f:e\to c,g:e\to d)$ where $e$ varies among the objects of $\cal C$ (we write $(f, g)\in R(e)$ to mean that $(f, g)\in R$ and $\textup{dom}(f)=\textup{dom}(g)=e$) satisfying the following properties: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item for any arrow $k:e'\to e$, if $(f,g)\in R$ then $(f\circ k, g\circ k)\in R$; \item for any $e\in {\cal C}$ and any arrows $x:e\to c, y:e\to d$, if $\{f:e'\to e \mid\ (x\circ f, y\circ f)\in R\}\in J(e)$ then $(x, y)\in R$; \item for any $e\in {\cal C}$ and any $(x, y), (x', y')\in R(e)$, if $x=x'$ then $\{f:e'\to e \mid y\circ f=y'\circ f\}\in J(e)$; \item for any $e\in {\cal C}$ and any $x:e\to c$, $\{f:e'\to e \mid \exists y:e'\to d \text{ such that } (x\circ f, y)\in R(e') \}\in J(e)$; \end{enumerate} \item the composite $S\ast R$ of two arrows $R:c\to d$ and $S:d\to a$ is given by the following formula: \begin{equation*}\begin{split} (S\ast R)(e)&=\{(x:e\to c, z:e\to a) \mid \{f:e'\to e \mid \exists y:e'\to d\, \\ & \quad\quad(x\circ f, y)\in R(e')\textup{ and } (y, z\circ f)\in S(e')\}\in J(e) \} \end{split}\end{equation*} for any $e\in {\cal C}$. \end{itemize} One half of the equivalence ${\cal C}_{J}\simeq a_{J}({\cal C})$ is given by the functor ${\cal C}_{J}\to a_{J}({\cal C})$ acting on objects by sending any $c\in {\cal C}_{J}$ to $l(c)$ and any arrow $R:c\to c'$ in ${\cal C}_{J}$ to the arrow $l(c)\to l(c')$ in $a_{J}({\cal C})$ whose graph is $a_{J}(R)$.
nodes.label: corfullsubcategorytopos

nodes.name: Relating the local and the relational description of arrows
nodes.statement: Let us clarify the relationship between the description of arrows in $a_{J}({\cal C})$ given by Proposition \ref{propexplicit} with that provided by Corollary \ref{corfullsubcategorytopos} (modulo the equivalence $a_{J}({\cal C})\simeq {\cal C}_{J}$). We stress that, unlike the former description (as equivalence classes of ways of representing them), the latter is \emph{canonical}; in particular, the composition operation, not being defined by using representatives, does not require any choices. Indeed, $J$-functional relations \emph{are} equivalence classes themselves. Given an arrow $R:c\to d$ in ${\cal C}_{J}$, by property (iv) we have (by taking $e=c$ and $x$ equal to the identity arrow on $c$) that $S:=\{f:e\to c \mid \exists y:e\to d \text{ such that } (f, y)\in R \}\in J(c)$. By using the axiom of choice, we can therefore choose, for each $f\in S$, an arrow $y_{f}:e\to d$ such that $(f, y_{f})\in R$, and hence the family $\{f:e\to c, y_{f}:e\to d \mid f\in S\}$ presents the arrow $l(c)\to l(d)$ corresponding to $R$ in the sense of Proposition \ref{propexplicit}. In the converse direction, we claim that, given a family ${\cal F}=\{f:\textup{dom}(f)\to c, g_{f}:\textup{dom}(f) \to d \mid f\in S\}$ inducing an arrow $\xi:l(c)\to l(d)$ in the sense of Proposition \ref{propexplicit} (we present $\cal F$ in the form of Remark \ref{rempropexplicit}(b) for simplicity), the $J$-functional relation $R$ corresponding to the arrow $\xi$ admits the following explicit description: $$ (h,k)\in R \quad\text{if and only if}\quad \text{ for all } \chi\in h^{\ast}(S), k\circ \chi\equiv_{J} g_{h\circ \chi} $$ By definition of $R$ as the pullback of the graph of the arrow $\xi:l(c)\to l(d)$ along the arrow $\eta_{y_{\cal C}(c)}\times \eta_{y_{\cal C}(d)}$, $R$ is characterized by the following universal property: for any $e\in {\cal C}$, $(h,k)\in R(e)$ if and only if $\xi\circ l(h)=l(k)$. Now, since the sieve $S$ is $J$-covering, for any $h$, the sieve $h^{\ast}(S)$ is $J$-covering as well and hence the family of arrows $\{l(\chi) \mid \chi\in h^{\ast}(S)\}$ is epimorphic on $l(e)$. So $\xi\circ l(h)=l(k)$ if and only if $\xi\circ l(h)\circ l(\chi)=l(k)\circ l(\chi)$ for every $\chi\in h^{\ast}(S)$. But $\xi\circ l(h)\circ l(\chi)=\xi\circ l(h\circ \chi)=l(g_{h\circ \chi})$, while $l(k)\circ l(\chi)=l(k\circ \chi)$, so $\xi\circ l(h)\circ l(\chi)=l(k)\circ l(\chi)$ if and only if $l(g_{h\circ \chi})=l(k\circ \chi)$, i.e. if and only if $k\circ \chi\equiv_{J} g_{h\circ \chi}$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: The canonical relational description of arrows $l(c)\to l(d)$ versus the local representation of Proposition 2.5; explicit translation formula.
nodes.label: remrelationstwoapproaches

nodes.name: Site description of the subcategory of sheafified sieves
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site. Then the full subcategory of ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ on the objects of the form $a_{J}(S)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$ and $S$ a ($J$-closed) sieve on $c$ is equivalent to the category ${\cal C}_{J}^{s}$ defined as follows: \begin{itemize} \item the objects of ${\cal C}_{J}^{s}$ are the pairs $(c, S)$ consisting of an object $c$ of $\cal C$ and a ($J$-closed) sieve $S$ on $c$; \item the arrows $(c, S)\to (d, T)$ are the collections $R$ of pairs of arrows $(x:e\to c,y:e\to d)$ where $e$ varies among the objects of $\cal C$ (we write $(x, y)\in R(e)$ to mean that $(x, y)\in R$ and $\textup{dom}(x)=\textup{dom}(y)=e$) satisfying the following properties: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item for any $(x,y)\in R$, $x\in S$ and $y\in T$; \item for any arrow $f:e'\to e$, if $(x,y)\in R$ then $(x\circ f, y\circ f)\in R$; \item for any $e\in {\cal C}$ and any $(x:e\to c, y:e\to d)\in S\times T$, if $\{f:e'\to e \mid\ (x\circ f, y\circ f)\in R\}\in J(e)$ then $(x,y)\in R$; \item for any $e\in {\cal C}$ and any $(x, y), (x', y')\in R(e)$, if $x=x'$ then $\{f:e'\to e \mid y\circ f=y'\circ f\}\in J(e)$; \item for any $e\in {\cal C}$ and any $x:e\to c$ in $S$, $\{f:e'\to e \mid \exists y:e'\to d \text{ such that } (x\circ f, y)\in R(e') \}\in J(e)$; \end{enumerate} \item the composite $R'\ast R:(c, S)\to (a, Z)$ of two arrows $R:(c, S)\to (d, T)$ and $R':(d, T)\to (a, Z)$ is given by the following formula: \begin{equation*}\begin{split} (R'\ast R)(e)&=\{(x:e\to c, z:e\to a)\in S\times Z \mid \{f:e'\to e \mid \exists y:e'\to d\, \\ & \quad\quad(x\circ f, y)\in R(e')\textup{ and } (y, z\circ f)\in R'(e')\}\in J(e) \} \end{split}\end{equation*} for any $e\in {\cal C}$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Objects $a_J(S)$ for sieves $S$ form a category equivalent to ${\cal C}^s_J$ of pairs $(c,S)$ with $J$-functional relations as arrows.
assumptions: $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site
conclusions: the full subcategory of ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ on the objects of the form $a_{J}(S)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$ and $S$ a ($J$-closed) sieve on $c$ is equivalent to the category ${\cal C}_{J}^{s}$ defined as follows: \begin{itemize} \item the objects of ${\cal C}_{J}^{s}$ are the pairs $(c, S)$ consisting of an object $c$ of $\cal C$ and a ($J$-closed) sieve $S$ on $c$; \item the arrows $(c, S)\to (d, T)$ are the collections $R$ of pairs of arrows $(x:e\to c,y:e\to d)$ where $e$ varies among the objects of $\cal C$ (we write $(x, y)\in R(e)$ to mean that $(x, y)\in R$ and $\textup{dom}(x)=\textup{dom}(y)=e$) satisfying the following properties: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item for any $(x,y)\in R$, $x\in S$ and $y\in T$; \item for any arrow $f:e'\to e$, if $(x,y)\in R$ then $(x\circ f, y\circ f)\in R$; \item for any $e\in {\cal C}$ and any $(x:e\to c, y:e\to d)\in S\times T$, if $\{f:e'\to e \mid\ (x\circ f, y\circ f)\in R\}\in J(e)$ then $(x,y)\in R$; \item for any $e\in {\cal C}$ and any $(x, y), (x', y')\in R(e)$, if $x=x'$ then $\{f:e'\to e \mid y\circ f=y'\circ f\}\in J(e)$; \item for any $e\in {\cal C}$ and any $x:e\to c$ in $S$, $\{f:e'\to e \mid \exists y:e'\to d \text{ such that } (x\circ f, y)\in R(e') \}\in J(e)$; \end{enumerate} \item the composite $R'\ast R:(c, S)\to (a, Z)$ of two arrows $R:(c, S)\to (d, T)$ and $R':(d, T)\to (a, Z)$ is given by the following formula: \begin{equation*}\begin{split} (R'\ast R)(e)&=\{(x:e\to c, z:e\to a)\in S\times Z \mid \{f:e'\to e \mid \exists y:e'\to d\, \\ & \quad\quad(x\circ f, y)\in R(e')\textup{ and } (y, z\circ f)\in R'(e')\}\in J(e) \} \end{split}\end{equation*} for any $e\in {\cal C}$. \end{itemize}
nodes.label: corhyperconnectedsieves

nodes.name: Geometric categories and ${\cal C}^s_J$
nodes.statement: If $\cal C$ is a geometric category (i.e. a well-powered category which has finite limits, images of arrows which are stable under pullback and arbitrary unions of subobjects that are stable under pullback) and $J$ is the geometric topology on it (whose covering sieves are those which contain small families of arrows the union of whose images is the given object) then $\cal C$ is closed under subobjects in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$, so the category ${\cal C}_{J}^{s}$ is equivalent to $\cal C$.
nodes.statement_short: For a geometric category with the geometric topology, ${\cal C}^s_J$ is equivalent to $\cal C$.
nodes.label: remsubcanonicalclosedsubobjects

nodes.name: Mono/epi criteria for arrows induced by $J$-functional relations
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a $J$-functional relation from $P$ to $Q$ in $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ and $\alpha_{R}:a_{J}(P)\to a_{J}(Q)$ the arrow in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $R$. Then \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $\alpha_{R}$ is a monomorphism if and only if for any $c\in {\cal C}$ and any elements $(x,y), (x',y')\in R(c)$ such that $y=y'$, the sieve $\{f:d\to c \mid P(f)(x)=P(f)(x')\}$ is $J$-covering. \item $\alpha_{R}$ is an epimorphism if and only if for any $c\in {\cal C}$ and $y\in Q(c)$, the sieve $\{f:d\to c \mid (\exists x\in P(d))((x, Q(f)(y))\in R(d))\}$ is $J$-covering. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Explicit local criteria for $\alpha_R$ to be a monomorphism or an epimorphism.
assumptions: $R$ be a $J$-functional relation from $P$ to $Q$ in $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ and $\alpha_{R}:a_{J}(P)\to a_{J}(Q)$ the arrow in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $R$
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $\alpha_{R}$ is a monomorphism if and only if for any $c\in {\cal C}$ and any elements $(x,y), (x',y')\in R(c)$ such that $y=y'$, the sieve $\{f:d\to c \mid P(f)(x)=P(f)(x')\}$ is $J$-covering. \item $\alpha_{R}$ is an epimorphism if and only if for any $c\in {\cal C}$ and $y\in Q(c)$, the sieve $\{f:d\to c \mid (\exists x\in P(d))((x, Q(f)(y))\in R(d))\}$ is $J$-covering. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: propfunctionalrelationmonoepi

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.18 (Mono/epi criteria for arrows induced by $J$-functional relations)
nodes.statement: Given an arrow $\alpha:A\to B$ in a topos and its graph $R_{\alpha}\rightarrowtail A\times B$, $\alpha$ is a monomorphism (resp. an epimorphism) if and only if $\pi_{B}:R_{\alpha}\to B$ is a monomorphism (resp. an epimorphism). But by Lemma \ref{lemmalift}, $\alpha_{R}$ is a monomorphism if and only if for every $c\in {\cal C}$ and any elements $(x,y), (x',y')\in R(c)$ such that $y=y'$, the sieve $\{f:d\to c \mid P(f)(x)=P(f)(x')\}$ is $J$-covering, while $\alpha_{R}$ is an epimorphism if and only if for any $c\in {\cal C}$ and $y\in Q(c)$, the sieve $\{f:d\to c \mid (\exists x\in P(d))((x, Q(f)(y)\in R(d))) \}$ is $J$-covering.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce mono/epi of $\alpha_R$ to the projection from its graph and apply Lemma 2.1.

nodes.name: Explicit description of the associated sheaf
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site. Then \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item An arrow $\xi:l(c)\to a_{J}(P)$ in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ (equivalently, an element of $a_{J}(P)(c)$) can be identified with an equivalence class of families $\{x_{f}\in P(\textup{dom}(f)) \mid f\in S\}$ of elements of $P$ indexed by the arrows $f$ of a $J$-covering sieve $S$ on $c$ which are \emph{locally matching} in the sense that for any arrow $g$ composable with an arrow $f\in S$, $x_{f\circ g}\equiv_{J} P(g)(x_{f})$, modulo the equivalence which identifies two such families when they are locally equal on a common refinement. \item Any such family yields a local representation of $\xi$ in the sense that $\xi\circ l(f)=r_{x_{f}}$ for each $f\in S$, where $r_{x_{f}}$ is the image under $a_{J}$ of the arrow $y_{\cal C}(\textup{dom}(f))\to P$ corresponding to the element $x_{f}\in P(\textup{dom}(f))$ via the Yoneda lemma. \item Alternatively, the elements of $a_{J}(P)(c)$ can be identified with functions sending to each arrow $f:d\to c$ in $\cal C$ a (possibly empty) $\equiv_{J}$-equivalence class $C_{f}\subseteq P(\textup{dom}(f))$ of elements of $P(\textup{dom}(f))$ in such a way that \begin{itemize} \item for any $g$ composable with $f$, $P(g)(C_{f})\subseteq C_{f\circ g}$; \item for any $y\in P(\textup{dom}(f))$, if $\{g:\textup{dom}(g)\to \textup{dom}(f) \mid P(g)(y)\in C_{f\circ g}\}\in J(\textup{dom}(f))$ then $y\in C_{f}$; \item $\{g:\textup{dom}(g)\to \textup{dom}(f) \mid C_{f\circ g}\neq \emptyset \}\in J(\textup{dom}(f))$. \end{itemize} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Elements of $a_J(P)(c)$ are classes of locally matching families on covering sieves, or functorial assignments of $\equiv_J$-classes.
assumptions: $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item An arrow $\xi:l(c)\to a_{J}(P)$ in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ (equivalently, an element of $a_{J}(P)(c)$) can be identified with an equivalence class of families $\{x_{f}\in P(\textup{dom}(f)) \mid f\in S\}$ of elements of $P$ indexed by the arrows $f$ of a $J$-covering sieve $S$ on $c$ which are \emph{locally matching} in the sense that for any arrow $g$ composable with an arrow $f\in S$, $x_{f\circ g}\equiv_{J} P(g)(x_{f})$, modulo the equivalence which identifies two such families when they are locally equal on a common refinement. \item Any such family yields a local representation of $\xi$ in the sense that $\xi\circ l(f)=r_{x_{f}}$ for each $f\in S$, where $r_{x_{f}}$ is the image under $a_{J}$ of the arrow $y_{\cal C}(\textup{dom}(f))\to P$ corresponding to the element $x_{f}\in P(\textup{dom}(f))$ via the Yoneda lemma. \item Alternatively, the elements of $a_{J}(P)(c)$ can be identified with functions sending to each arrow $f:d\to c$ in $\cal C$ a (possibly empty) $\equiv_{J}$-equivalence class $C_{f}\subseteq P(\textup{dom}(f))$ of elements of $P(\textup{dom}(f))$ in such a way that \begin{itemize} \item for any $g$ composable with $f$, $P(g)(C_{f})\subseteq C_{f\circ g}$; \item for any $y\in P(\textup{dom}(f))$, if $\{g:\textup{dom}(g)\to \textup{dom}(f) \mid P(g)(y)\in C_{f\circ g}\}\in J(\textup{dom}(f))$ then $y\in C_{f}$; \item $\{g:\textup{dom}(g)\to \textup{dom}(f) \mid C_{f\circ g}\neq \emptyset \}\in J(\textup{dom}(f))$. \end{itemize} \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: propsheafification

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.19 (Explicit description of the associated sheaf)
nodes.statement: The proof of (i) and (ii) is a straightforward generalisation of that of Proposition \ref{propexplicit}, while part (iii) follows at once from Theorem \ref{thmfunctionalrelations} and Proposition \ref{propfuncionalassignment}.
nodes.statement_short: Straightforward generalisation of Proposition 2.5; part (iii) from Theorem 2.13 and Proposition 2.12.

nodes.name: Sheafification without the plus construction
nodes.statement: Proposition \ref{propsheafification}(i) gives an explicit description of the associated sheaf functor $a_{J}(P)$ of a presheaf $P$, different from the usual construction of it by means of the double plus construction. This alternative construction of the associated sheaf functor seems to have been first discovered (albeit not published) by Eduardo Dubuc in the eighties.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 2.19(i) gives a construction of $a_J(P)$ alternative to the double plus construction, attributed to Dubuc.

nodes.name: Canonical arrow $\tilde{\alpha}$ between colimits of representables
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $F:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ and $F:{\cal A}'\to {\cal C}$ two functors to $\cal C$ related by a functor $\xi:{\cal A}\to {\cal A}'$ and a natural transformation $\alpha:F\to F'\circ \xi$. We have an arrow \[ \tilde{\alpha}: \textup{colim}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(y_{\cal C}\circ F) \to \textup{colim}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(y_{\cal C}\circ F') \] in $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$, defined through the universal property of the colimit by setting \[ \tilde{\alpha} \circ \lambda_{a}= \chi_{\xi(a)}\circ y_{\cal C}(\alpha(a)) \] (for any $a\in {\cal A}$), where $\lambda_{a}:y_{\cal C}(F(a))\to \textup{colim}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(y_{\cal C}\circ F)$ (for $a\in {\cal A}$) and $\chi_{a'}:y_{\cal C}(F'(a'))\to \textup{colim}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(y_{\cal C}\circ F')$ (for $d'\in {\cal A}'$) are the canonical colimit arrows.
nodes.statement_short: For $(\xi,\alpha)$ relating $F$ and $F'$, the induced arrow between colimits of $y_{\cal C}\circ F$ and $y_{\cal C}\circ F'$.

nodes.name: Well-posedness of $\tilde{\alpha}$ and the relations $R_c$
nodes.statement: To show that this definition is indeed well-posed, we recall that colimits in functor categories are computed pointwise; so, for each $c\in {\cal C}$, we have \[ \textup{colim}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(y_{\cal C}\circ F)(c)=(\coprod_{a\in {\cal A}}\textup{Hom}_{\cal C}(c, F(a)))\slash R_{c}, \] where $R_{c}$ is the equivalence relation given by: $(x:c\to F(a), x':c\to F(b))\in R_{c}$ if and only if $x$ and $x'$ belong to the same connected component of the category $(c\downarrow F)$. Similarly, we have \[ \textup{colim}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(y_{\cal C}\circ F')(c)=(\coprod_{a'\in {\cal A}'}\textup{Hom}_{\cal C}(c, F(a')))\slash R'_{c}, \] where $R'_{c}$ is the equivalence relation given by: $(y:c\to F(a'), y':c\to F(b'))\in R'_{c}$ if and only if $y$ and $y'$ belong to the same connected component of the category $(c\downarrow F')$. We thus see that the arrows $\{\chi_{\xi(a)}\circ y_{\cal C}(\alpha(a)) \mid a\in {\cal A}\}$ form indeed a cocone under the diagram $y_{\cal C}\circ F$, since they respect these equivalence relations.
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise description of the colimits via equivalence relations $R_c$, $R'_c$ of connected components, showing $\tilde\alpha$ is well defined.

nodes.name: Derivation of the relative cofinality criterion
nodes.statement: We want to understand under which conditions the arrow $\tilde{\alpha}$ is sent by the associated sheaf functor $a_{J}:[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }] \to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ to an isomorphism. For this, we can use Lemma \ref{lemmalift}(iii); this yields the following result:
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 2.1(iii) to the arrow $\tilde\alpha$.

nodes.name: Relative cofinality criterion
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $F:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ and $F':{\cal A}'\to {\cal C}$ two functors to $\cal C$ related by a functor $\xi:{\cal A}\to {\cal A}'$ and a natural transformation $\alpha:F\to F'\circ \xi$. Then the canonical arrow \[ \tilde{\alpha}: \textup{colim}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(y_{\cal C}\circ F) \to \textup{colim}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(y_{\cal C}\circ F') \] defined above is sent by $a_{J}$ to an isomorphism \[ a_{J}(\tilde{\alpha}): \textup{colim}_{{\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)}(l\circ F) \to \textup{colim}_{{\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)}(l\circ F) \] if and only if $(\xi, \alpha)$ satisfies the following ` cofinality' conditions: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item For any object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any arrow $y:c\to F'(a')$ in $\cal C$ there are a $J$-covering family $\{f_i: c_i \to c \mid i\in I\}$ and for each $i\in I$ an object $a_{i}$ of $\cal A$ and an arrow $y_i:c_{i}\to F(a_{i})$ such that $(y\circ f_{i}, \alpha(a_{i})\circ y_{i})\in R'_{c_{i}}$. \item For any object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any arrows $x:c\to F(a)$ and $x':c\to F(b)$ in $\cal C$ such that $(\alpha(a)\circ x, \alpha(b)\circ x')\in R'_{c}$ there is a $J$-covering family $\{f_i: c_i \to c \mid i\in I\}$ such that $(x\circ f_i, x'\circ f_i)\in R_{c_{i}}$ for each $i\in I$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $a_J(\tilde\alpha)$ is an isomorphism iff $(\xi,\alpha)$ satisfies two local cofinality conditions.
assumptions: $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $F:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ and $F':{\cal A}'\to {\cal C}$ two functors to $\cal C$ related by a functor $\xi:{\cal A}\to {\cal A}'$ and a natural transformation $\alpha:F\to F'\circ \xi$
conclusions: the canonical arrow \[ \tilde{\alpha}: \textup{colim}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(y_{\cal C}\circ F) \to \textup{colim}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(y_{\cal C}\circ F') \] defined above is sent by $a_{J}$ to an isomorphism \[ a_{J}(\tilde{\alpha}): \textup{colim}_{{\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)}(l\circ F) \to \textup{colim}_{{\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)}(l\circ F) \] if and only if $(\xi, \alpha)$ satisfies the following ` cofinality' conditions: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item For any object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any arrow $y:c\to F'(a')$ in $\cal C$ there are a $J$-covering family $\{f_i: c_i \to c \mid i\in I\}$ and for each $i\in I$ an object $a_{i}$ of $\cal A$ and an arrow $y_i:c_{i}\to F(a_{i})$ such that $(y\circ f_{i}, \alpha(a_{i})\circ y_{i})\in R'_{c_{i}}$. \item For any object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any arrows $x:c\to F(a)$ and $x':c\to F(b)$ in $\cal C$ such that $(\alpha(a)\circ x, \alpha(b)\circ x')\in R'_{c}$ there is a $J$-covering family $\{f_i: c_i \to c \mid i\in I\}$ such that $(x\circ f_i, x'\circ f_i)\in R_{c_{i}}$ for each $i\in I$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: procofinality

nodes.name: Morphism of fibrations $\alpha_{\textup{fib}}$
nodes.statement: Then the natural transformation $\alpha$ yields a functor $\alpha_{\textup{fib}}: (1_{\cal C}\downarrow F) \to (1_{\cal C}\downarrow F')$, sending to each object $(c, a, x:c\to F(a))$ of $(1_{\cal C}\downarrow F)$ the object $(c, \xi(a), \alpha(a)\circ x:c\to F'(\xi(a)))$ of $(1_{\cal C}\downarrow F')$, which is actually a morphisms of fibrations.

nodes.name: Remarks on the relative cofinality conditions
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item Condition (i) of Proposition \ref{procofinality} can be replaced by the single condition that for any object $u:=(c, a', y:c\to F'(a'))$ of the category $(1_{\cal C}\downarrow F')$, there is a $J$-covering family such that the category $((u\circ f_{i})\downarrow \alpha_{\textup{fib}})$ is non-empty for each $i\in I$. \item In condition (i) of Proposition \ref{procofinality}, if the claim is satisfied for an arrow $y:d\to F(a')$ then it is satisfied by any arrow of the form $y\circ z$ for an arrow $z$ composable with $y$. It follows in particular that if $\xi$ is essentially surjective and $\alpha$ is the identity then the condition is satisfied. \item Proposition \ref{procofinality} can be notably applied in the context of colimit-preserving functors $$Z:{\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)\to {\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K)$$ between Grothendieck toposes such that $Z\circ l=l'\circ z$ for some functor $z:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ (such as, for instance, inverse image functors of geometric morphisms induced by a morphism of sites, or essential images of essential geometric morphisms induced by a continuous comorphism of sites, as investigated in section \ref{sec:essentialmorphismsandcomorphisms}). Indeed, the value of such a functor $Z$ on a $J$-sheaf $Q$ on $\cal C$ is given by $\textup{colim}_{{\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K)}(Z\circ l \circ \pi_{Q})=\textup{colim}_{{\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K)}(l'\circ z \circ \pi_{Q})$, where $\pi_{Q}:{\int Q} \to {\cal C}$ is the canonical projection functor from the category $\int Q$ of elements of $Q$. See section \ref{sec:locallyconnectedmorphisms} below for an application of this remark. \item We shall see in section \ref{sec:essentialmorphismsandcomorphisms} (cf. Proposition \ref{propcofinalcontinuous}) that, under the hypotheses of Proposition \ref{procofinality}, if $p$ is a continuous comorphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ such that the essential image of the associated geometric morphism $C_{p}$ is conservative then $(\xi, \alpha)$ satisfies the conditions of Proposition \ref{procofinality} if and only if $(\xi, p\alpha)$ does. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Reformulations of the cofinality conditions via $\alpha_{\rm fib}$, stability, and application to colimit-preserving functors.
nodes.label: rempropcofinality

nodes.name: Two applications of the relative cofinality criterion
nodes.statement: Let us now apply Proposition \ref{procofinality} in two notable cases: \begin{enumerate}[(1)] \item $F=\xi:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$, $F'=1_{\cal C}$, $\alpha$ is the identity. In this case the equivalence relations $R'_{c}$ are the total relations, and the proposition yields the following criterion: the canonical arrow \[ \textup{colim}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(y_{\cal C}\circ \xi) \to \textup{colim}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(y_{\cal C})=1_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]} \] is sent by $a_{J}$ to an isomorphism \[ \textup{colim}_{{\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)}(l\circ \xi) \to 1_{{\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)} \] if and only if the following conditions are satisfied: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item For any object $c$ of $\cal C$ there are a $J$-covering family $\{f_i: c_i \to c \mid i\in I\}$ and for each $i\in I$ an object $a_{i}$ of $\cal A$ and an arrow $y_i:c_{i}\to F(a_{i})$. \item For any object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any arrows $x:c\to F(a)$ and $x':c\to F(b)$ in $\cal C$, there is a $J$-covering family $\{f_i: c_i \to c \mid i\in I\}$ such that $(x\circ f_i, x'\circ f_i)\in R_{c_{i}}$ for each $i\in I$. \end{enumerate} Notice that if $J$ is the trivial Grothendieck topology then the above conditions amount precisely to the requirement that for every object $c$ of $\cal C$, the category $(c\downarrow \xi)$ be non-empty and connected, which means precisely that the functor $F$ is cofinal (in the classical sense). It is therefore natural to call \emph{$J$-cofinal} a functor $F:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ which satisfies the two conditions above (see Definition \ref{defrelcofinality} below). \item $F'$ is the forgetful functor $U_{c_{0}}:{\cal C}\slash c_{0}\to {\cal C}$ for an object $c_{0}$ of $\cal C$, $\xi$ is a cocone $\{\xi_{a}: F(a)\to c_{0} \mid a\in {\cal A}\}$ under the functor $F$ with vertex $c_{0}$ and $\alpha$ is the identity. In this case we have: for any $y:c \to (U_{c_{0}}([p:c'\to c_{0}]))$ and $y':c \to (U_{c_{0}}([q:c''\to c_{0}]))$, $(y, y')\in R'_{c}$ if and only if $p\circ y=q\circ y'$. So the proposition yields the following criterion: the cocone $\xi$ is sent by the canonical functor ${\cal C}\to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ to a colimit if and only if the following conditions are satisfied: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item For any object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any arrow $y:c\to c_{0}$ in $\cal C$ there are a $J$-covering family $\{f_i: c_i \to c \mid i\in I\}$ and for each $i\in I$ an object $a_{i}$ of $\cal A$ and an arrow $y_i:c_{i}\to F(a_{i})$ such that $y\circ f_{i}=\xi_{a_{i}}\circ y_{i}$. \item For any object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any arrows $x:c\to F(a)$ and $x':c\to F(b)$ in $\cal C$ such that $\xi_{a}\circ x= \xi_{b}\circ x'$ there is a $J$-covering family $\{f_i: c_i \to c \mid i\in I\}$ such that $(x\circ f_i, x'\circ f_i)\in R_{c_{i}}$ for each $i\in I$. \end{enumerate} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Specialize Proposition 2.21 to $F'=1_{\cal C}$ (giving $J$-cofinality) and to a cocone over a slice.

nodes.name: $J$-cofinal functor
nodes.statement: Given a small site $({\cal C}, J)$, a functor $F:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ is said to be \emph{$J$-cofinal} if the following conditions are satisfied: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item For any object $c$ of $\cal C$ there are a $J$-covering family $\{f_i: c_i \to c \mid i\in I\}$ and for each $i\in I$ an object $a_{i}$ of $\cal A$ and an arrow $y_i:c_{i}\to F(a_{i})$. \item For any object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any arrows $x:c\to F(a)$ and $x':c\to F(b)$ in $\cal C$ there is a $J$-covering family $\{f_i: c_i \to c \mid i\in I\}$ such that $x\circ f_i$ and $x'\circ f_i$ belong to the same connected component of the category $(c_i \downarrow F)$ for each $i\in I$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: A functor into a site that is locally non-empty and locally connected in the sense of comma categories.
nodes.label: defrelcofinality

nodes.name: Characterization of $J$-cofinal functors
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $F:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ a functor. Then $F$ is $J$-cofinal if and only if the canonical arrow \[ \textup{colim}_{{\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)}(l\circ F) \to 1_{{\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)} \] is an isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: $F$ is $J$-cofinal iff the colimit of $l\circ F$ is terminal in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C},J)$.
assumptions: $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $F:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ a functor
conclusions: $F$ is $J$-cofinal if and only if the canonical arrow \[ \textup{colim}_{{\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)}(l\circ F) \to 1_{{\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)} \] is an isomorphism.
equivalent_conditions: $F$ is $J$-cofinal
the canonical arrow
nodes.label: corcofinalcharacterization

nodes.name: Reduction of colimit preservation to slice cofinality
nodes.statement: Given a functor $D:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ and a cocone $\{\xi_{a}: D(a)\to c_{0} \mid a\in {\cal A}\}$ under $D$ with vertex $c_{0}$, we can lift $D$ to a functor $D_{\xi}:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}\slash c_{0}$ such that $U_{c_{0}}\circ D_{\xi}=D$. Let $J_{c_{0}}$ be the Grothendieck topology on ${\cal C}\slash c_{0}$ whose covering sieves are precisely those whose image under $U_{c_{0}}$ is $J$-covering. Then the arrow \[ \textup{colim}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(y_{\cal C}\circ D) \to \textup{colim}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(y_{\cal C}\circ U_{c_{0}})\cong y_{\cal C}(c_{0}) \] induced by $\xi$, regarded as an arrow in $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }] \slash y_{\cal C}(c_{0})$, corresponds to the unique arrow \[ \textup{colim}_{[({{\cal C}\slash c_{0}})^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]}(y_{({\cal C}\slash c_{0})}\circ D_{\xi}) \to 1_{[{({\cal C}\slash c_{0})}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]} \] and hence the image of the former under $a_{J}$ corresponds to the image of the latter under $a_{J_{c_{0}}}$ via the equivalence ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)\slash l(c_{0}) \simeq {\bf Sh}({\cal C}\slash c_{0}, J_{c_{0}})$. So the cocone $\xi$ is sent by the canonical functor ${\cal C}\to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ to a colimit if and only if $D_{\xi}$ is $J_{c_{0}}$-cofinal:
nodes.statement_short: Lift $D$ to the slice ${\cal C}/c_0$ and use ${\bf Sh}({\cal C},J)/l(c_0)\simeq{\bf Sh}({\cal C}/c_0,J_{c_0})$.

nodes.name: Colimits in a sheaf topos via relative cofinality
nodes.statement: Let $D:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ be a functor and $\xi$ a cocone $\{\xi_{a}: D(a)\to c_{0} \mid a\in {\cal A}\}$ under $D$ with vertex $c_{0}$. Then $\xi$ is sent by the canonical functor $l:{\cal C}\to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ to a colimit cocone if and only if the functor $D_{\xi}$ is $J_{c_{0}}$-cofinal, equivalently if and only if the following conditions are satisfied: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item For any object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any arrow $y:c\to c_{0}$ in $\cal C$ there are a $J$-covering family $\{f_i: c_i \to c \mid i\in I\}$ and for each $i\in I$ an object $a_{i}$ of $\cal A$ and an arrow $y_i:c_{i}\to D(a_{i})$ such that $y\circ f_{i}=\xi_{a_{i}}\circ y_{i}$. \item For any object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any arrows $x:c\to D(a)$ and $x':c\to D(b)$ in $\cal C$ such that $\xi_{a}\circ x= \xi_{b}\circ x'$ there is a $J$-covering family $\{f_i: c_i \to c \mid i\in I\}$ such that $x\circ f_i$ and $x'\circ f_i$ belong to the same connected component of the category $(c_{i} \downarrow D)$ for each $i\in I$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $l$ sends a cocone to a colimit iff the lifted functor $D_\xi$ is $J_{c_0}$-cofinal, made explicit by two local conditions.
assumptions: $D:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ be a functor and $\xi$ a cocone $\{\xi_{a}: D(a)\to c_{0} \mid a\in {\cal A}\}$ under $D$ with vertex $c_{0}$
conclusions: $\xi$ is sent by the canonical functor $l:{\cal C}\to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ to a colimit cocone if and only if the functor $D_{\xi}$ is $J_{c_{0}}$-cofinal, equivalently if and only if the following conditions are satisfied: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item For any object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any arrow $y:c\to c_{0}$ in $\cal C$ there are a $J$-covering family $\{f_i: c_i \to c \mid i\in I\}$ and for each $i\in I$ an object $a_{i}$ of $\cal A$ and an arrow $y_i:c_{i}\to D(a_{i})$ such that $y\circ f_{i}=\xi_{a_{i}}\circ y_{i}$. \item For any object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any arrows $x:c\to D(a)$ and $x':c\to D(b)$ in $\cal C$ such that $\xi_{a}\circ x= \xi_{b}\circ x'$ there is a $J$-covering family $\{f_i: c_i \to c \mid i\in I\}$ such that $x\circ f_i$ and $x'\circ f_i$ belong to the same connected component of the category $(c_{i} \downarrow D)$ for each $i\in I$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: corcolimitintopos

nodes.name: Colimits in a Grothendieck topos via generalized elements
nodes.statement: Let $D:{\cal A}\to {\cal E}$ be a functor from a small category $\cal A$ to a Grothendendieck topos $\cal E$ and $\xi$ a cocone $\{\xi_{a}: D(a)\to e_{0} \mid a\in {\cal A}\}$ under $D$ with vertex $e_{0}$. Then $\xi$ is a colimit cocone if and only if the functor $D_{\xi}$ is $({J^{\textup{can}}_{\cal E}})_{e_{0}}$-cofinal, equivalently if and only if the following conditions are satisfied: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item For any object $e$ of $\cal E$ and any arrow $y:e\to e_{0}$ in $\cal E$ there are an epimorphc family $\{f_i: e_i \to e \mid i\in I\}$ in $\cal E$ and for each $i\in I$ an object $a_{i}$ of $\cal A$ and an arrow $y_i:e_{i}\to D(a_{i})$ such that $y\circ f_{i}=\xi_{a_{i}}\circ y_{i}$. \item For any object $e$ of $\cal E$ and any arrows $x:e\to D(a)$ and $x':e\to D(b)$ in $\cal E$ such that $\xi_{a}\circ x= \xi_{b}\circ x'$ there is an epimorphic family $\{f_i: e_i \to e \mid i\in I\}$ in $\cal E$ such that $x\circ f_i$ and $x'\circ f_i$ belong to the same connected component of the category $(e_{i} \downarrow D)$ for each $i\in I$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: A cocone in a topos is a colimit iff it is locally surjective and locally connected on generalized elements.
assumptions: $D:{\cal A}\to {\cal E}$ be a functor from a small category $\cal A$ to a Grothendendieck topos $\cal E$ and $\xi$ a cocone $\{\xi_{a}: D(a)\to e_{0} \mid a\in {\cal A}\}$ under $D$ with vertex $e_{0}$
conclusions: $\xi$ is a colimit cocone if and only if the functor $D_{\xi}$ is $({J^{\textup{can}}_{\cal E}})_{e_{0}}$-cofinal, equivalently if and only if the following conditions are satisfied: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item For any object $e$ of $\cal E$ and any arrow $y:e\to e_{0}$ in $\cal E$ there are an epimorphc family $\{f_i: e_i \to e \mid i\in I\}$ in $\cal E$ and for each $i\in I$ an object $a_{i}$ of $\cal A$ and an arrow $y_i:e_{i}\to D(a_{i})$ such that $y\circ f_{i}=\xi_{a_{i}}\circ y_{i}$. \item For any object $e$ of $\cal E$ and any arrows $x:e\to D(a)$ and $x':e\to D(b)$ in $\cal E$ such that $\xi_{a}\circ x= \xi_{b}\circ x'$ there is an epimorphic family $\{f_i: e_i \to e \mid i\in I\}$ in $\cal E$ such that $x\circ f_i$ and $x'\circ f_i$ belong to the same connected component of the category $(e_{i} \downarrow D)$ for each $i\in I$. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Continuity and cofinality
nodes.statement: Let $A:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ be a functor and $v:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal C}', J')$ a continuous functor (that is, a weak morphism of sites). If $A$ is $J$-cofinal then it satisfies, together with the identical natural transformation on $v\circ F$, the conditions of Proposition \ref{procofinality}. Moreover, the converse holds if ${\bf Sh}(v)^{\ast}$ reflects isomorphisms.
nodes.statement_short: $J$-cofinal functors satisfy the cofinality conditions after composing with a continuous functor; conversely if ${\bf Sh}(v)^*$ reflects isos.
assumptions: $A:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ be a functor and $v:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal C}', J')$ a continuous functor (that is, a weak morphism of sites)
conclusions: If $A$ is $J$-cofinal then it satisfies, together with the identical natural transformation on $v\circ F$, the conditions of Proposition \ref{procofinality}.
Moreover, the converse holds if ${\bf Sh}(v)^{\ast}$ reflects isomorphisms.
If $A$ is $J$-cofinal then it satisfies, together with the identical natural transformation on $v\circ F$, the conditions of Proposition \ref{procofinality}.
Moreover, the converse holds if ${\bf Sh}(v)^{\ast}$ reflects isomorphisms.

nodes.label: propcontinuitycofinality

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.27 (Continuity and cofinality)
nodes.statement: Since $v$ is continuous, the following square commutes: $$ \xymatrix{ {\cal C} \ar[r]^{v} \ar[d]_{l_{{\cal C}}} & {\cal C}' \ar[d]^{l_{\cal C}'} \\ {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J) \ar[r]^{{\bf Sh}(v)^{\ast}} & {\bf Sh}({\cal C}', J') } $$ By Corollary \ref{corcofinalcharacterization}, $F$ is $J$-cofinal if and only if the unique arrow \[ \textup{colim}_{{\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)}(l_{\cal C}\circ F) \to 1_{{\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)} \] is an isomorphism. Since $(C_{v})_{!}$ is colimit-preserving and the above square commutes, we have \[ {\bf Sh}(v)^{\ast}(\textup{colim}_{{\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)}(l_{\cal C}\circ F))\cong \textup{colim}_{{\bf Sh}({{\cal C}'}, J')}(l_{{\cal C}'}\circ v\circ F) \] and \[ {\bf Sh}(v)^{\ast}(1_{{\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)})=\textup{colim}_{{\bf Sh}({{\cal C}'}, J')}(l_{{\cal C}'}\circ v) \] So if the above arrow is an isomorphism then the canonical arrow \[ \textup{colim}_{{\bf Sh}({{\cal C}'}, J')}(l_{{\cal C}'}\circ v\circ F) \to \textup{colim}_{{\bf Sh}({{\cal C}'}, J')}(l_{{\cal C}'}\circ v) \] induced by $F$ is an isomorphisms (that is, $F$ satisfies the conditions of Proposition \ref{procofinality} together with the identical natural transformation on $v\circ F$), and the converse holds if ${\bf Sh}(v)^{\ast}$ reflects isomorphisms.
nodes.statement_short: Translate cofinality via Corollary 2.24 and apply the colimit-preserving inverse image.

nodes.name: Adjunction $L_A\dashv R_A$ induced by a functor into a topos
nodes.statement: Recall that any functor $A:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ from an essentially small category $\cal C$ to a Grothendieck topos $\cal E$ induces an adjuction $(L_{A} \dashv R_{A})$, where $R_{A}:{\cal E}\to [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ is the ` hom' functor $\textup{Hom}_{\cal E}(A(-),-)$ and $L_{A}:[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }] \to {\cal E}$ is the unique (up to isomorphism) colimit-preserving functor which extends $A$ along the Yoneda embedding $y_{\cal C}:{\cal C}\to [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$, in other words, the left Kan extension of $A$ along the Yoneda embedding $y_{\cal C}:{\cal C}\to [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$, which sends each presheaf $P$ on $\cal C$ to the colimit of the diagram $A\circ \pi_{P}$, where $\pi_{P}:{\int P} \to {\cal C}$ is the canonical projection from the category ${\int P}$ of elements of $P$ (see, for instance, section I.5 of \cite{MM}).
nodes.statement_short: $R_A=\mathrm{Hom}_{\cal E}(A(-),-)$ and $L_A$ the left Kan extension of $A$ along Yoneda.

nodes.name: Flat functor
nodes.statement: The functor $A$ is said to be \emph{flat} if $L_{A}$ preserves finite limits.

nodes.name: Diaconescu's equivalence
nodes.statement: If $J$ is a Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$ and $A$ is flat then the geometric morphism $(L_{A}\dashv R_{A}):{\cal E}\to [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ factors through the canonical geometric inclusion ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)\hookrightarrow [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ if and only if $A$ is $J$-continuous.
